design:
Decision: approval keeps its meaning (the reviewer's verdict that lets the work start landing); "done" is derived from approval plus the task's landing record reaching `landed` (landing_queue.LANDED, with landed_sha). No new task status and no extra step: the operator ruled out adding one.

Decision: the change replaces the approval-as-finish checks rather than adding another patch beside them. The F1113 "flow outlives its finished build" special case becomes unnecessary once a build is not finished until its tasks land; the builder removes what is now dead rather than leaving it beside the new rule. AW-124 was dropped (operator, 2026-11-13) and is not to be re-merged.

Decision: prerequisite gating is unchanged. A dependent task still starts when its prerequisite is approved and brings in the prerequisite's work, as today ("Bring in prerequisite work" commits). Waiting for landing there would serialise every chain behind the landing queue.

Decision (operator, 2026-11-13): a build that lands as a pull request is done when the PR is merged; a build that lands nowhere is done at approval, since nothing will ever merge.

open_questions.question: Builds that do not land on main: is done = PR merged for pull-request builds, and done = approved for builds that land nowhere?

problem:
Today everything treats approval as the finish line. A build is marked finished when every task is approved or rejected (hub/hub/builds.py:1206 finish_if_done), its progress counts approved tasks as done (builds.py:195), and TERMINAL_STATUSES is {approved, rejected} (task_transition_service.py:1500). Landing — the project's checks on main, then the merge — runs afterwards and can still send work back.

What that cost on 2026-11-13:
- The Changes-tab build (SPSCT) was marked finished at 11:24 and left Running. At 11:40 its landing failed on main and sent SPSCT-2 back. The build looked done while it was broken, and the operator lost track of it.
- AW-124 was approved at 14:12 and sent back by its landing at 14:41 (merge conflict). On the board it read as finished for half an hour.
- The code has grown patches around the gap: the flow outliving its finished build (F1113, builds.py:1229 loop_has_open_work), and AW-124 (dropped by the operator in favour of this change), which tried to show a finished build in Running while its flow lives.

The operator (2026-11-13): "Once it's merged and on master then we consider it done." There is no new step: landing is the final step, and it already exists.

requirements.rationale: Landing can still fail after approval (SPSCT-2 at 11:40, AW-124 at 14:41 on 2026-11-13); calling such work done hides it from the operator.
requirements.statement: A task counts as done only when it is approved and its work has landed on the project's main branch; an approved task whose landing is queued, being checked, held, or sent back is not done.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-13: the landing is the final step and already exists.
requirements.statement: Reaching done requires no action beyond what landing already does: no new task status, operator click or agent turn is introduced between a landing that lands and the task being done.
A build is marked finished only when every one of its tasks is done or rejected; while any approved task in it has not landed, the build stays running.
A build's progress counts as done only tasks that are done, and shows approved tasks that have not landed as a separate 'landing' count.

A flow set to stop when its queue empties stops only once every one of its tasks is done or rejected; a landing that sends a task back finds the flow still running and the task is picked up by its next firing.

The Running tab lists a build until it is finished, and for each approved task that has not landed shows its landing state (waiting, being checked, held, or sent back with the reason the landing gave).
A task card on the board distinguishes an approved task that has landed from one that has not, naming the landing state of the latter.

requirements.rationale: Otherwise builds that finished under the old rule before the change keep hiding unlanded work.
requirements.statement: A build already marked finished whose approved tasks include one that has not landed is shown as running again, without operator action, the first time the Hub evaluates it after this change ships.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-13: a lands-nowhere build will never merge, so waiting for a merge would keep it running forever.
requirements.statement: For a task in a build that lands as a pull request, done means the pull request was merged; for a task in a build that lands nowhere, done means approved.

in_scope: When a build is finished, and what its progress counts as done
When a flow whose stop condition is an emptied queue stops
What the Running tab lists, and the landing state it shows for each approved task
How a task card on the board shows an approved task that has not landed
Builds already marked finished whose approved tasks have not landed
non_goals: A new task status or a new step after landing: landing is the last step
Changing when a dependent task may start: it still starts on its prerequisite's approval
Changing what landing does: the checks it runs, how it batches, or how it sends work back
Changing who may approve, or what approval requires (evidence, review)
Deploying or restarting a Hub after the merge: "on main" is the finish line, not "running somewhere"

summary: Approval stays the reviewer's verdict, but "done" moves to "approved and landed on the project's main branch". A build finishes, its flow stops, and its progress counts a task as done only once that task's landing reached main. Until then the build stays in Running and shows where each approved task is in landing.
